title: 1968 AHSME Problem 34
statement: With \(400\) members voting, the House of Representatives defeated a bill. A re-vote, with the same members voting, resulted in passage of the bill by twice the margin by which it was originally defeated. The number voting for the bill on the re-vote was \(\dfrac{12}{11}\) of the number voting against it originally. How many more members voted for the bill the second time than voted for it the first time?

solutions.text:
Let \(F,\) \(G\) be the original and second numbers voting for the bill. The ratio condition gives \(G=\frac{12}{11}(400-F).\) The passage margin is twice the original defeat margin, so \(2G-400=2(400-2F),\) or \(G+2F=600.\) Solving gives \(F=180,\) \(G=240,\) so \(60\) more members voted for it.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let the original and second numbers voting for be \(F\) and \(G\)
